explanation: cpop counts the bits of a word in one instruction, yet the loop around it still loads, xors, counts and adds one word per iteration. The second code spends more instructions on a step - shifts, masks and a multiplication - but each of them works on 32 words at once: eight 128-bit registers grouped together hold 32 lanes. It executes about a tenth of the instructions of the first. A special instruction for one word loses to ordinary instructions over a vector.
